Mixed sampling changes the training objective unless corrected: uniform negatives encourage broad discrimination; lexical neighbors emphasize separating similar items. Google’s [Mixed Negative Sampling](https://research.google/pubs/mixed-negative-sampling-for-learning-two-tower-neural-networks-in-recommendations/) combines uniform and batch negatives, while [Rawat et al.](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v139/rawat21a/rawat21a.pdf) show that sampling and weighting induce different implicit losses. Applied here, target-dependent lexical sampling should be described as a deliberately biased contrastive surrogate unless its actual sampling mechanism is accounted for; lexical similarity alone does not establish that an unobserved item is irrelevant.

For independent draws with replacement, use the complete conditional mixture q(j|history,target)=αq_uniform+(1−α)q_lexical, normalized after exclusions. An importance-sampled partition estimate keeps the positive contribution exact and weights each negative contribution by 1/(Kq). After deduplication or sampling without replacement, per-draw q generally is insufficient: use each item’s inclusion probability π(j|history,target), giving a negative-total estimate Σ_unique exp(score_j)/π_j. For K independent mixture draws followed by deduplication, π_j=1−(1−q_j)^K; fixed quotas, rejection, and refill rules require their own probabilities. These are sampling-design deductions consistent with [TensorFlow’s distinction between probabilities and expected counts](https://www.tensorflow.org/extras/candidate_sampling.pdf).

An unbiased partition estimate does not imply an unbiased log-loss or gradient because normalization and logarithms are nonlinear. [Correcting the LogQ Correction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331) also stresses that the positive is inserted deterministically. Practical choices: retain an explicitly biased hard-negative objective, or implement sampling-aware partition correction with full negative support and acknowledge finite-sample bias. Simple −log q does not automatically recover the candidate-classification posterior when sampling depends on the target.
